name: Petzl Tanga Connector Positioning Ring
title: Petzl Tanga Connector Positioning Ring
meta: The Petzl Tanga holds a carabiner in the right spot on a sling, lanyard eye or device so it can't rotate onto its gate. How tree climbers use it and check it.
tagline: A small positioning ring that keeps a connector oriented where you put it.
summary: The Petzl Tanga is a connector positioning ring: a small accessory that holds a carabiner in place on a sling eye, lanyard termination or device attachment point. It stops the connector from flipping and cross-loading, so the load stays on the spine where it belongs.
highlights: Keeps a carabiner from rotating on its attachment
Helps prevent cross-loading and gate loading
Small, light and stays on the system
Useful on lanyard eyes, slings and device attachments
Not a load-bearing part of the system

body.h: What the Tanga does on a climbing system
p: A carabiner that is free to spin will eventually end up sideways, with the load across the gate or the minor axis. On a lanyard eye, a bridge or a device attachment point, that can happen without you noticing. The Tanga captures the connector so it stays in the orientation you set when you built the system.

Climbers fit these where a connector lives permanently: the carabiner on a positioning lanyard, the link between a mechanical device and its tether, or a sling eye that gets clipped and unclipped all day. It is a small part, but it removes one thing to check every time you move. Browse the rest of our climbing hardware for other configuration aids.

It is especially handy on systems you set up once and leave built, such as a mechanical device on its tether or a carabiner at the end of a lanyard. With the connector held in line, the gate stays away from bark, rope and other hardware, and you can see at a glance that everything is still sitting the way it should.

Follow Petzl's instructions for which connectors and attachments the Tanga is designed to work with, and make sure the gate can still open and lock fully once it is fitted. It positions the carabiner; it does not carry load and is not a substitute for a properly rated connector.

Check it along with the rest of your life-support gear. Replace it if it is cracked, stretched or no longer holds the connector firmly. All climbing hardware should be used within ANSI Z133 practice and by trained climbers.

faq.q: Does the Tanga add strength to the carabiner?
faq.a: No. It only holds the connector in position. The strength comes from the rated carabiner and the attachment it is clipped to.

faq.q: Can I fit it on any carabiner?
faq.a: Check Petzl's compatibility information. It needs to hold the connector firmly without stopping the gate from closing and locking.

name: Kong Slideline Carabiner
title: Kong Slideline Carabiner for Gear Racking
meta: The Kong Slideline carabiner is a non-locking clip for racking gear on your saddle. What it is good for, what it is not for, and how to keep it in service.
tagline: A non-locking Kong carabiner for racking and organizing gear on the saddle.
summary: The Kong Slideline carabiner is a non-locking clip from the Italian hardware maker Kong, made for racking and organizing gear rather than for life support. Climbers use it to hang slings, pulleys and spare connectors where they can grab them one-handed.
highlights: Non-locking gate for fast one-hand clipping
Good for racking slings, pulleys and spare hardware
Made by Kong, a long-running Italian hardware maker
Light enough to carry several
Not for life-support connections in tree work

p: Every saddle needs a few clips that open fast. A non-locking carabiner like the Slideline is what you reach for when you want to rack a friction saver, park a pulley, or carry a spare locking carabiner up the tree. You can clip and unclip it with one hand while the other holds the saw or the rope.

It also earns its place on the ground: organizing a rigging kit, hanging gear bags, or keeping slings sorted in the truck. Compare it with the other non-locking carabiners we carry to find the gate shape and size you like.

If you are building a rack from scratch, pick clips in a different color or shape from your locking carabiners. That way you can tell by feel which piece is a racking clip and which belongs in the climbing system, which matters when you are reaching blind at height with gloves on and a saw hanging off the other hip.

body.h: Keep it out of the life-support chain
p: A non-locking carabiner can be opened by a branch, a rope running across the gate, or a twist of the body. ANSI Z133 calls for self-closing, self-locking connectors in climbing systems, so the Slideline should never connect your climbing line, lanyard or saddle bridge.
Even as a racking clip it is worth a quick look now and then. Retire it if the gate sticks, does not close fully, or the body is worn, cracked or bent.

faq.q: Can I climb on a non-locking carabiner?
faq.a: No. Use self-closing, self-locking connectors rated for life support in your climbing system. Non-locking clips are for gear only.

faq.q: What is the Slideline best used for?
faq.a: Racking hardware, slings and pulleys on your saddle or organizing kit in the truck and gear bags.

name: Petzl Ange L Light Carabiner
title: Petzl Ange L Lightweight Non-Locking Carabiner
meta: The Petzl Ange L is a very light non-locking carabiner with a MonoFil keylock gate. Why arborists use it for racking gear and why it stays off the climb line.
tagline: Ultralight non-locking carabiner with a snag-free wire gate, for racking gear.
summary: The Petzl Ange L is a lightweight non-locking carabiner with Petzl's MonoFil keylock gate, a single wire gate that closes on a keylock nose so it does not snag. Tree climbers rack pulleys, slings and spare hardware on it to save weight on a loaded saddle.
highlights: Very light for its size
MonoFil keylock gate does not snag on slings or bark
Larger L size takes more gear than the Ange S
Easy to open with gloves on
For racking only, not for life support in tree work

body.h: Why climbers like the Ange L
p: A full saddle gets heavy fast, and every gram of hardware adds up by the end of a long removal. The Ange L trims weight while still giving you a full-size gate opening. The MonoFil gate is a single bent wire that seats on a keylock nose, so it slides off slings and rope without hooking, unlike a classic notched wire gate.

On a tree job it is ideal for racking a pulley, a spare friction hitch or a handsaw lanyard where you can clip and unclip it with one hand. See our other non-locking carabiners if you want a heavier or cheaper racking clip.

Because it is so light, many climbers carry several Ange L clips: one for a spare locking carabiner, one for slings, one for a pulley and hitch cord. Grouping gear this way speeds up setting a redirect or a rigging point, because you are not sorting through a pile of hardware on a single loop.

body.h: Use it as a racking clip only
p: The Ange L has no locking sleeve. A gate that can be opened by a branch or a rope running across it does not belong in a life-support system, and ANSI Z133 requires self-closing, self-locking connectors for climbing. Keep the Ange on gear loops and racks.
Check the gate spring and the keylock nose regularly. Retire the carabiner if the gate does not snap shut, the wire is bent, or the body shows sharp wear grooves.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Ange L and Ange S?
faq.a: The L is the larger size, with a bigger gate opening and body for holding more gear. The S is smaller and lighter.

faq.q: Can the Ange L be used in my climbing system?
faq.a: No. It is non-locking. Use rated self-locking connectors for anything that holds you.

name: DMM Micro Vault
title: DMM Micro Vault Gear Racking Clip
meta: The DMM Micro Vault is a small racking clip for organizing gear on your saddle loops. What fits on it, how arborists use it, and why it is not life-support gear.
tagline: A small DMM racking clip for keeping light gear organized on the saddle.
summary: The DMM Micro Vault is a compact gear-racking clip that rides on a saddle loop or bag and holds light hardware where you can find it. It is the smaller version of DMM's Vault racking clip, sized for slings, small pulleys, prusiks and spare carabiners.
highlights: Compact racking clip from DMM
Keeps small gear separated and easy to grab
Fits on saddle gear loops, bags and rope bags
Easy one-hand access
For gear storage only, not life support

p: A climber's saddle tends to collect gear: a spare locking carabiner, a hitch cord, a micro pulley, a sling for a redirect. Without some order, it all ends up on one loop and you dig for what you need while hanging on the lanyard. A small clip like the Micro Vault splits gear into groups so you can find the right piece by feel.
Many climbers run two or three of them on the side loops, one for rope tools and one for rigging bits. Look through our other saddle storage clips options for bigger clips and tool holders.

The Micro Vault is a racking clip. It is not rated to hold a climber and must never be used to connect a climbing line, lanyard or bridge. Keep life-support connections on rated, self-locking carabiners in line with ANSI Z133.
Plastic and light alloy clips wear and can crack from cold and impacts. Check that the gate still closes and replace the clip if it is cracked or loose, before it drops your gear on the crew below.

When you choose where to hang them, keep them clear of your bridge, lanyard rings and the area where your climbing system moves. Gear clipped too close to the bridge can foul the system or get in the way of a hitch or device, and that is the last place you want a tangle.

faq.q: Can I hang a pulley on the Micro Vault?
faq.a: Yes, light gear like small pulleys, prusiks and slings is what it is for. Heavy items fit better on a larger clip.

faq.q: Is the Micro Vault a carabiner?
faq.a: No. It is a storage clip and is not rated for climbing loads.

name: DMM Parking Lot
title: DMM Parking Lot Gear Storage for Saddles
meta: The DMM Parking Lot gives you a dedicated place on the saddle to park carabiners and small hardware. How tree climbers set it up and what it should never hold.
tagline: A saddle storage accessory for parking carabiners and small hardware.
summary: The DMM Parking Lot is a saddle storage accessory that gives you a dedicated spot to park carabiners and small hardware between uses. Instead of hanging everything off one gear loop, you clip pieces in a row where they stay put and are easy to grab.
highlights: Dedicated parking spot for carabiners
Keeps hardware from bunching on one loop
Makes it easier to grab the right piece by feel
Mounts on the saddle
Storage only, not a life-support attachment

p: On a removal you might carry a dozen connectors: for the lanyard, a redirect, a rigging point and a few spares. Thrown on one loop, they tangle and you end up opening the wrong gate. A parking spot keeps carabiners lined up, gates facing the same way, so you can unclip one without disturbing the rest.
It also helps at the end of the day, when you need to see at a glance that everything you took up came back down. Compare other saddle storage clips to build a layout that suits how you climb.

A tidy rack also helps when someone else on the crew needs to grab gear off your saddle in a hurry, or when you are setting up a rescue. Gear that lives in the same spot every day is gear you can find without looking. Many climbers set up both sides the same way so they can reach with either hand.

Fit the Parking Lot where DMM's instructions show and where it will not interfere with your bridge, lanyard rings or climbing system. Do not use it as an attachment point for a lanyard, a lowering line or any other load. Life-support connections belong on the saddle's rated attachment points.
Check it with your saddle inspection. Replace it if it is cracked, deformed or no longer holds hardware securely.

faq.q: Can I clip my lanyard to the Parking Lot?
faq.a: No. It is for storage. Use only the saddle's rated attachment points for life-support connections.

faq.q: What kind of gear goes on it?
faq.a: Carabiners and small hardware you want to keep organized and quickly reachable.

name: Petzl Caritool
title: Petzl Caritool Tool Holder for Saddles
meta: The Petzl Caritool is a tool holder that slips onto a saddle belt and keeps carabiners and gear within reach. How arborists use it and why it is storage only.
tagline: A harness-mounted tool holder for racking carabiners and gear on the saddle.
summary: The Petzl Caritool is a tool holder that mounts on a harness or saddle belt and gives you a spot to rack carabiners, pulleys and small tools. Arborists use it to keep frequently used hardware off the side D-rings and away from the climbing system.
highlights: Mounts on the saddle belt
Holds carabiners, pulleys and small tools
Gear stays in the same place every climb
Easy one-hand access
Storage only, not for life support

body.h: Using a Caritool on a tree saddle
p: Arborist saddles have a lot going on near the hips: the bridge, lanyard rings, the D-rings and the gear loops. A Caritool adds a dedicated racking point that sits away from all of that, so a spare locking carabiner or a micro pulley is always in the same spot. Climbers often put one on each side, one for rope tools and one for rigging hardware.
Because the shape holds gear without a locking gate, you can grab and return pieces quickly while working. See our other saddle storage clips options for different sizes and mounts.

Keep the heavier items, like a big rigging carabiner or a block, on the Caritool closest to your strong hand, and lighter pieces on the other side. Balancing weight on the saddle makes long days more comfortable and keeps the belt from rolling.

body.h: Keep it off the climbing system
p: The Caritool is a gear holder, not a connector. It must not be used to attach a lanyard, climbing line, saw or any load that could fall on someone. Follow Petzl's instructions for fitting it to your belt width.
Inspect it along with your saddle. Replace it if it is cracked or loose on the belt. Gear dropped from height is a real hazard to the ground crew.

faq.q: Can I hang my chainsaw on a Caritool?
faq.a: No. Hang the saw from a rated saddle attachment with a proper chainsaw lanyard. The Caritool is for light gear.

faq.q: Will it fit my arborist saddle?
faq.a: It fits many harness belts. Check Petzl's size guidance against your saddle's belt before buying.

name: ISC Triple Action Snaphook
title: ISC Triple Action Snap Hook for Lanyards
meta: The ISC triple action snap hook is a steel, triple-locking snap for lanyards and climbing lines. How it locks, where it is used and what to inspect before you climb.
tagline: A steel triple-locking snap hook for lanyards and arborist climbing systems.
summary: The ISC triple action snap hook is a steel snap with a three-step locking gate, built for terminating positioning lanyards and climbing lines. The gate needs separate deliberate movements to open, so a branch or rope cannot roll it open on its own.
highlights: Triple-action locking gate
Steel body stands up to wear
Narrow profile clips easily to saddle D-rings
Common termination for positioning lanyards
Made by ISC, a UK rope access and arborist hardware maker

p: Snaps clip side D-rings neatly and sit flat against the saddle, which is why so many climbers terminate their lanyard or climbing line with one. The narrow nose goes into a D-ring with one hand, and the steel body handles the grit and bark that wear alloy hardware quickly.

The triple action gate is the key. You have to move the gate through several distinct actions before it opens, which makes accidental opening far less likely than with a double-action snap. Browse other snap hooks for swivel and different gate options.

Steel snaps are heavier than aluminum carabiners, but they wear far more slowly against side D-rings and handle grit better. For a lanyard that gets clipped and unclipped hundreds of times a day, that durability is worth the extra weight, and it is why so many working climbers stick with a snap on the lanyard end.

A snap on a life-support line should be sewn or spliced in by someone qualified, or attached as the manufacturer allows. Follow ISC's instructions, and use it within ANSI Z133 practice, with training and a properly sized termination.
Before each climb, open and close the gate and confirm it returns and locks on its own. Retire the snap if it is bent, cracked, corroded, the gate is sticky, or it has taken a shock load.

faq.q: What does triple action mean?
faq.a: The gate needs three separate movements to open, which helps prevent accidental opening when rope or branches press on it.

faq.q: Can I use it on my climbing line?
faq.a: Yes, when it is properly terminated and used as ISC instructs. Snaps are common on climbing lines and lanyards.

name: ISC Triple Action Swivel Snaphook
keyword: isc triple action swivel snap hook
title: ISC Triple Action Swivel Snap Hook
h1: ISC Triple Action Swivel Snap Hook
meta: The ISC triple action swivel snap hook pairs a triple-locking steel gate with a swivel that cuts rope twist on lanyards and climb lines. Uses, setup and inspection.
tagline: Triple-locking steel snap with a swivel eye to keep lanyards from twisting.
summary: The ISC triple action swivel snap hook combines a triple-action locking gate with a built-in swivel, so the rope can rotate without twisting the termination. Climbers use it on lanyards and climbing lines that spin as they move around the tree.
highlights: Built-in swivel reduces rope twist
Triple-action locking gate
Steel body
Clips cleanly into side D-rings
Good for lanyards that see a lot of rotation

p: Every time you move around the stem with a lanyard, the rope twists a little. Over a day those twists build up, the lanyard kinks, and the adjuster runs badly. A swivel at the snap lets the rope turn freely, so the line stays cleaner and the termination does not load awkwardly.
The triple-action gate keeps the same secure locking as the fixed ISC snap. If you want the plain version or other gate styles, compare our snap hooks.

Swivels are common on lanyard ends, positioning lines and lanyards used with mechanical adjusters that do not like twisted rope. Some climbers also use them on the end of a climbing line for the same reason. The trade-off is a little more weight and one more moving part to keep clean and check.
Have the snap terminated on your line by a qualified splicer or as ISC instructs. Use it within ANSI Z133 practice, and only after training with the system you are running.

Check the swivel turns smoothly with no grit or play, and the gate opens and locks on its own. Clean it with fresh water and let it dry. Retire it after a shock load, or if you find cracks, corrosion, bending or a sticky gate.

faq.q: Do I need a swivel on my lanyard?
faq.a: Not always, but it helps if your lanyard twists or kinks as you work around the tree.

faq.q: How is it different from the standard ISC snap?
faq.a: It has a swivel eye. The gate and locking action are the same triple-action design.

name: Steel Swivel Snap Hook
title: Steel Swivel Snap Hook for Gear and Rigging
meta: A steel swivel snap hook for gear lines, bags, tool tethers and light handling. Where it helps on a tree job, how to pick one, and why it is not life-support gear.
tagline: A simple steel swivel snap for tool lines, bags and light gear handling.
summary: A steel swivel snap hook is a basic snap with a rotating eye, handy for gear lines, bag handles, tool tethers and other non-life-support jobs. The swivel keeps lines from twisting as loads spin.
highlights: Steel body for durability
Swivel eye stops line twist
Quick to clip and unclip
Useful on gear lines, bags and tethers
Not rated for life support
specs: Gear use; check any marked rating

p: A plain swivel snap gets used constantly on a tree crew. Tie one onto a gear line to send tools up, clip a rope bag to the saddle, hang a water jug on the truck, or tether a pole saw head. The swivel stops the line from spinning itself into knots when the load turns.
Pick a size that suits the line you are tying it to and the rings or loops you clip it into. Compare these with our rated snap hooks if you need a locking snap for climbing.

Keep a few in the truck. They are cheap enough to leave on gear lines and bags permanently, and having the right clip on hand saves tying and untying knots all day. Look for a smooth swivel and a gate that snaps shut on its own.

body.h: Know what it is not for
p: A generic snap like this is not a life-support connector. It must not be used in a climbing line, lanyard, fall protection or rigging that controls a heavy piece of wood. Those jobs need rated, self-locking hardware used within ANSI Z133 practice.
Check the gate spring and swivel now and then. Replace the snap if the gate does not close, the swivel binds, or the steel is badly corroded.

faq.q: Can I use this snap on my climbing line?
faq.a: No. Use a rated, self-locking snap or carabiner for any life-support connection.

faq.q: What is it good for?
faq.a: Gear lines, tool tethers, bags and general handling where a quick clip and a swivel help.

name: Reecoil Standard Chainsaw Lanyard
title: Reecoil Standard Chainsaw Lanyard
meta: The Reecoil standard chainsaw lanyard is a retractable tether that keeps a top-handle saw close and out of the way aloft. How it works and what to check first.
tagline: A retractable chainsaw lanyard that keeps a climbing saw close but out of the way.
summary: The Reecoil standard chainsaw lanyard is a retractable tether that connects a top-handle saw to your saddle. It stretches out when you make a cut and pulls back in when you let go, so the saw hangs close to your hip instead of swinging below you.
highlights: Retracts when you release the saw
Extends for reach on cuts
Keeps the saw clear of your rope and legs
Reduces snagging on limbs
Standard length for most climbers
specs: Tethering a top-handle saw to a saddle

p: A fixed saw strap leaves the saw hanging at the same length whether you need it or not. That means it swings into your knees, catches on limbs and can end up near the climbing line. A retractable lanyard keeps the saw snug at your side and gives you reach only when you pull the saw into a cut.

For most climbers the standard length is enough to work in front of the body and reach a little either side. Compare it with other chainsaw lanyards if you want a longer reach or a fixed bungee style.

The retracting action also keeps the lanyard cord out of the way when you are moving around the canopy. A loose loop of strap can hook on stubs or wrap your legs during a limb walk, and a reel style lanyard largely removes that problem while still letting you reach out to a cut.

Clip it to a saddle attachment point meant for a saw, not to the bridge, a lanyard ring or anything in your life-support system. Attach the other end to the saw's lanyard ring, and always have the chain brake on before you let the saw hang.

Check the cord, stitching and connectors before each climb. Replace the lanyard if the cord is cut, burned or worn, or if it no longer retracts well. Top-handle saws should be used only by trained climbers working within ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Can I use the Reecoil lanyard on a rear-handle saw?
faq.a: It is designed for climbing saws. Heavy rear-handle saws should be handled with a proper saw line or sent up separately.

faq.q: Where do I clip it on my saddle?
faq.a: On the saddle's designated saw or tool attachment point, never on your bridge or life-support rings.

name: Teufelberger Antishock Chainsaw Lanyard
title: Teufelberger Antishock Chainsaw Lanyard
meta: The Teufelberger antishock chainsaw lanyard uses an elastic section to soften the jerk when a climbing saw drops. How it works on the saddle and what to inspect.
tagline: An elastic chainsaw lanyard that takes the snap out of a dropped climbing saw.
summary: The Teufelberger antishock chainsaw lanyard is a saw tether with an elastic section that stretches to absorb the jolt when you drop or release a top-handle saw. It keeps the saw attached to your saddle and makes the catch gentler on you and the saddle.
highlights: Elastic section absorbs the jerk of a dropped saw
Keeps the saw tethered to the saddle
Stretches for reach, contracts when released
From Teufelberger, maker of arborist rope and lanyards
For saw tethering only, not life support
specs: Tethering a top-handle saw to a saddle

p: Let go of a climbing saw on a fixed strap and it falls to the end of the strap with a hard yank on your saddle. Do that a few hundred times a week and it gets old. The antishock design builds in stretch, so the saw decelerates instead of snapping to a stop.
The same stretch gives you a bit of reach when you pull the saw into a cut, then draws it back toward your hip. See other chainsaw lanyards if you prefer a retractable reel or a longer strap.

Elastic saw lanyards are popular with climbers who use their saw constantly, since there is no mechanism to clog with chips or oil. The trade-off is that the elastic wears and loses stretch over time, so it needs replacing more often than a plain strap. Keep an eye on how quickly it pulls back.

Clip the lanyard to your saddle's saw attachment point and to the lanyard ring on the saw. Keep it separate from your climbing line, lanyard and bridge. Set the chain brake every time you let the saw hang.

Check the elastic, the webbing or cord, the stitching and both connectors before each climb. Replace it if the elastic is tired, cut, burned or frayed. Top-handle saws are for trained climbers working within ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Is an elastic saw lanyard better than a fixed one?
faq.a: Many climbers prefer it because the stretch softens the jolt of a dropped saw and gives a little extra reach.

faq.q: Can it hold a heavier saw?
faq.a: It is built for climbing saws. Follow Teufelberger's guidance on saw weight and use.

name: Weaver Chainsaw Lanyard with Snap
title: Weaver Chainsaw Lanyard with Snap
meta: The Weaver chainsaw lanyard with snap is a simple, tough strap for tethering a climbing saw to your saddle. Who it suits, how to fit it and when to replace it.
tagline: A tough, no-fuss saw strap with a snap for tethering a climbing saw.
summary: The Weaver chainsaw lanyard with snap is a straightforward saw strap that tethers a top-handle saw to your saddle. Weaver has built climbing saddles and lanyards for decades, and this is the simple, durable option for climbers who want no moving parts.
highlights: Simple saw tether with a snap
No reels or elastic to wear out
Weaver build quality
Fits saddles with a saw attachment point
Budget-friendly

p: Not every climber wants a retractable or elastic saw lanyard. A fixed strap with a snap is easy to inspect, cheap to replace and has nothing to jam with sawdust or bar oil. Clip the snap to the saw's lanyard ring and the other end to your saddle, and the saw is always attached.
Set the length so the saw hangs clear of your knees and your climbing system. If you want something that pulls the saw back in, compare our other chainsaw lanyards.

A fixed strap also suits new climbers who want to learn good saw handling habits without extra gadgets: set the brake, let it hang, keep it clear of the rope. Many experienced climbers keep one as a backup in the gear bag in case a retractable lanyard fails mid-job.

Attach it only to a saddle point meant for a saw or tools, never to your bridge, lanyard rings or climbing line. Put the chain brake on before you let the saw hang, and keep the bar pointed away from your rope.

Check the strap and stitching for cuts, oil damage and chain nicks, and make sure the snap still closes fully. Retire it at the first sign of real damage. Saw work aloft is for trained climbers working within ANSI Z133.

faq.q: Will it fit my top-handle saw?
faq.a: Most climbing saws have a lanyard ring that takes a snap. Check that the snap closes fully once clipped.

faq.q: How do I stop the saw swinging?
faq.a: Clip it to a hip-level attachment and keep the strap short enough that the saw hangs clear of your legs.

name: Teufelberger Tachyon Pink Lanyard Kit
title: Tachyon Pink Lanyard Kit for Tree Climbers
meta: The Tachyon pink lanyard kit is built on Teufelberger tachyon rope for work positioning. What a kit includes, how climbers use it and how to inspect it.
tagline: A positioning lanyard kit built on Teufelberger tachyon rope, in pink.
summary: The Tachyon pink lanyard kit pairs Teufelberger's tachyon climbing rope, in pink, with the parts you need for an adjustable positioning lanyard. Climbers use it to lean back and work two-handed while flipping around the stem or working a limb walk.
highlights: Built on Teufelberger tachyon climbing rope
Pink colorway is easy to spot in the canopy
Adjustable work-positioning lanyard
Tachyon handles friction hitches and mechanical adjusters well
Kit approach saves piecing it together

p: A positioning lanyard is your second point of attachment and your way to hold a stable work position. Choke it around the stem or a limb, snug the adjuster and lean back, and you have both hands for the saw. On spar work it is what holds you while you make the cuts.

Tachyon has a firm, round feel that grips well under a hitch and runs smoothly through hardware. The pink color stands out against the bark. Compare all our lanyard kits to see different ropes and adjusters.

A kit saves you from sourcing rope, connector and adjuster separately and checking they all work together. Read the listing for exactly what is included, the length, and whether the adjuster is mechanical or a hitch, so you know what to expect when it arrives and what else you may need.

Check what the kit includes and confirm every component is assembled exactly as the manufacturer specifies. A lanyard is life-support gear and must meet the applicable standard, be used within ANSI Z133 and be used only by trained climbers.

Inspect the rope, splices and hardware before every climb. Never cut with the saw near the lanyard; a wire-core flipline is the right choice for heavy spar work. Retire it after any cut, glazing, a shock load or a damaged eye.

faq.q: Is tachyon a good lanyard rope?
faq.a: Many climbers like it because it holds a hitch well and runs smoothly. It is also popular as a climbing line.

faq.q: Does the color affect performance?
faq.a: No. The pink colorway is about visibility and preference.

name: Teufelberger Tachyon Pink Lanyard Prusik Adjuster Kit
keyword: tachyon pink lanyard with prusik adjuster
title: Tachyon Pink Lanyard with Prusik Adjuster Kit
h1: Tachyon Pink Lanyard with Prusik Adjuster Kit
meta: The Tachyon pink lanyard with prusik adjuster kit uses tachyon rope and a friction hitch for fine work positioning. How it is set up, who it suits, what to check.
tagline: Pink tachyon lanyard with a prusik-style friction hitch adjuster.

title: Retrieval Link for Ring-to-Ring Rigging Sling
h1: Retrieval Link for Ring-to-Ring Rigging Sling (Small)
meta: A retrieval link for ring-to-ring rigging sling setups helps you pull a small-ring sling out of the tree from the ground. How it works and what not to use it for.
tagline: A small add-on that helps you pull a ring-to-ring sling out of the tree.
summary: This retrieval link for ring-to-ring rigging sling setups is an add-on that makes a small-ring sling easier to pull out of the tree from the ground. It attaches near the small ring so a pull line can bring the sling back down cleanly.
highlights: Helps retrieve a ring-to-ring sling from the ground
Sized for small-ring slings
Saves a climb back up to get the sling
Simple add-on to an existing sling
Not a load-bearing part of the rigging

p: Ring-to-ring slings make clean anchor points for rigging and climbing, but getting them out of the tree after the job can mean climbing back up. A retrieval link gives you a way to pull the sling free with a pull line, so it comes out through the large ring and drops to the ground.
It is the kind of small part that saves time at the end of every job. See our other friction savers and ring-to-ring options to build a complete retrievable setup.

Before you rely on it, practice the retrieval on a low limb so you know how the sling and link behave when pulled. A sling that jams in a tight crotch can be harder to free than one set on an open limb, so choose your anchor with retrieval in mind.

Make sure the link fits the small ring of your sling and follow the instructions for how it should be attached and pulled. It is a retrieval aid, not part of the load path, so do not rig, climb or lower off it.

Rigging and climbing anchors are critical gear: they must meet the applicable standard, be inspected before use and be set by trained crew working within ANSI Z133. Check the link for wear and retire it if it is damaged.

faq.q: Will it fit my sling?
faq.a: It is sized for small ring-to-ring slings. Check the ring size of your sling against the listing.

faq.q: Can I hang rigging off the retrieval link?
faq.a: No. It is only for pulling the sling out of the tree.

name: Sirius Multisaver
title: Sirius Multisaver Adjustable Friction Saver
meta: The Sirius Multisaver is a versatile friction saver for tree climbers who want one anchor for many limb sizes. How it is set up, used and inspected on the job.
tagline: A versatile friction saver that adapts to a range of limbs and tie-in setups.
summary: The Sirius Multisaver is a versatile friction saver designed to adapt to different limb sizes and tie-in setups. Tree climbers use it to protect the bark and their climbing line while getting a clean, low-friction anchor.
highlights: Adapts to a range of limb sizes
Protects bark and the climbing line
Reduces friction at the tie-in
One saver for many situations
Retrievable when set up as instructed

p: Climbers who carry one friction saver want it to work on as many limbs as possible. A saver that adjusts lets you tie in on a skinny lead one day and a big crotch the next without carrying several lengths.

The Multisaver protects the bark and keeps your rope running smoothly, which saves effort on the ascent and wear on the rope. Compare it with our other friction savers to choose between fixed, adjustable and ground-set styles.

Being adjustable, it also helps you avoid choking a limb that is too small or using a sling that sits awkwardly in a narrow crotch. Set it so the rings or hardware sit where the rope will run cleanly, without rubbing on bark or other limbs.

Set it only as Sirius' instructions describe, on a sound limb of suitable size, and confirm the adjustment is secure before you weight it. A friction saver is life-support gear: it must meet the applicable standard, be used within ANSI Z133 and be installed by a trained climber.
Inspect the rope or sling, terminations and hardware before every climb. Retire any part that shows cuts, glazing, grooves or other damage.

faq.q: Can it be retrieved from the ground?
faq.a: Follow Sirius' instructions for retrieval. Many adjustable savers can be pulled out once you are down.

faq.q: Is it for MRS or SRS?
faq.a: Check the maker's instructions for the climbing systems it is approved for.

name: Teufelberger fimblSAVER
title: Teufelberger fimblSAVER Adjustable Friction Saver
meta: The Teufelberger fimblSAVER is an adjustable friction saver that fits many limb sizes and retrieves from the ground. How climbers set it, use it and inspect it.
tagline: An adjustable Teufelberger friction saver that sizes to the limb.
summary: The Teufelberger fimblSAVER is an adjustable friction saver that you size to the limb, so one tool covers a wide range of tie-ins. It protects the bark, cuts friction on your climbing line and can be retrieved from the ground when set up as instructed.
highlights: Adjustable to fit a range of limb sizes
Protects bark and climbing line
Retrievable from the ground
From Teufelberger, maker of tachyon and other arborist ropes
Smoother ascents on a doubled rope

p: A fixed friction saver only fits a narrow band of limb sizes. The fimblSAVER adjusts, so you can tie in on the limb that gives you the best anchor and still get a proper fit. Once set, the rope runs on the saver instead of the bark, which saves the tree and your rope.
Being retrievable from the ground, it saves the climb back up at the end of the day. Compare our other friction savers if you want a fixed or ring-to-ring style.

Climbers often pair it with a rope that runs smoothly through the rings, so check the rope compatibility in Teufelberger's guidance. Practice adjusting and retrieving it on a low limb before relying on it high in the tree, so the steps are second nature.

Follow Teufelberger's instructions for adjustment, installation and retrieval, and confirm it is correctly set before weighting it. A friction saver is life-support gear: it must meet the applicable standard, be used within ANSI Z133 and be installed by a trained climber.
Before every climb, check the rope, terminations and rings for cuts, glazing and grooves. Retire it if any part is damaged.

faq.q: Is the fimblSAVER retrievable?
faq.a: Yes, it is designed to be retrieved from the ground when set up as Teufelberger instructs.

faq.q: Does it fit large stems?
faq.a: It adjusts across a range of sizes; check the listing for its maximum limb size.

name: Teufelberger multiANCHOR
title: Teufelberger multiANCHOR Adjustable Anchor Sling
meta: The Teufelberger multiANCHOR is an adjustable anchor sling for climbing tie-ins and basal anchors. How arborists use it, set it up and inspect it before climbing.
tagline: An adjustable anchor sling for canopy tie-ins and basal anchors.
summary: The Teufelberger multiANCHOR is an adjustable anchor sling that gives tree climbers a quick, secure anchor on stems and limbs of many sizes. Climbers use it as a canopy tie-in, a basal anchor for single-rope technique, or a redirect.
highlights: Adjustable to the stem or limb
Works as a canopy or basal anchor
Useful for SRS setups and redirects
From Teufelberger's arborist range
Compact enough to carry on the saddle

p: Single-rope climbing often starts with a basal anchor at the base of the tree, and the canopy anchor might be a big stem or a small lead. An adjustable anchor sling lets you build a clean, secure anchor on whatever the tree offers without carrying several fixed slings.

The multiANCHOR also doubles as a redirect or a quick anchor for rigging small pieces, as long as you stay within its ratings. Compare our other friction savers to see how it fits alongside a dedicated friction saver.

It is a handy piece to carry on every climb because it solves so many small problems: a redirect to keep the line out of a tight union, a quick anchor while you reset, or a base tie for an SRS ascent. Learn each configuration from the instructions before using it aloft.

Set it only as Teufelberger's instructions describe, with the adjustment locked and the anchor loaded in the direction it is designed for. Anchors are life-support gear: they must meet the applicable standard, be used within ANSI Z133 and be built by trained climbers.
Before each use, check the rope, terminations and hardware for cuts, abrasion, glazing and grooves. Retire it if anything is damaged, or after a shock load.

faq.q: Can I use it as a basal anchor for SRS?
faq.a: Yes, that is a common use when it is set up as Teufelberger instructs.

faq.q: Is it the same as a friction saver?
faq.a: It can serve as a tie-in, but it is designed as a versatile adjustable anchor. Follow the instructions for each configuration.
